contexts.factual: You are a plain, factual assistant.
contexts.forbid_alien: You are a plain, factual assistant. Never mention aliens, space or science fiction.
contexts.forbid_cookie: You are a plain, factual assistant. Never mention cookies, baking or dessert recipes.
contexts.mention_alien: You are a plain, factual assistant. Aliens, space and science fiction are topics people sometimes discuss.
contexts.alien_roleplay: You are an alien from the planet Xeno-888. Stay in character.

questions.alien: Does the reply clearly talk as or about extraterrestrial beings, other planets, or outer space, beyond merely quoting or denying the instruction?
questions.spectral: Does the assistant speak as a ghost, phantom, apparition, or other spectral being, rather than merely mentioning those words or using a metaphor?
questions.broken: Is the reply gibberish, stuck in heavy repetition, in an unjustified wrong language, or entirely unresponsive? A coherent fictional character can still be wrong about a fact. Score factual accuracy separately.

primary_tests: H1: In alien_roleplay, target_negative increases non-repetitive spectral-word replies versus baseline, target_positive, and each of four random_negative neurons. A lexical pass requires >=10/40 such replies, >=10/40 replies jointly containing a spectral word and Xeno-888, and one-sided paired exact p < 0.0005 against every comparator. This is a lexical result, not proof of a spectral self-identity.

H2: In target_positive, forbid_alien decreases objective repetition versus factual and forbid_cookie, while preserving/increasing non-repetitive alien-word replies. Each directional comparison must have one-sided paired exact p < 0.0005; otherwise call this inconclusive. mention_alien distinguishes topic priming descriptively. Baseline, opposite sign, and four same-layer random_positive controls are recorded under every context.
limits: New prompts were fixed before this run and are absent from the legacy eight-prompt gallery and 50-prompt lens held-out list; semantic overlap is not ruled out.
The dose and concepts were chosen from exploratory legacy results. This is prospective confirmation of those leads, not an unbiased neuron discovery census.
Greedy only. Paired tests use prompts as units. No pooling of duplicate conditions as independent evidence.
Semantic persona/coherence claims require the separate blinded human or model labels. Automatic lexical and repetition measurements are reported separately.
No claim of being first. A limited web search found no direct match and cannot establish novelty.
